newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-POLYGRAM HIT BY $90 MLN CHARGE.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-POLYGRAM HIT BY $90 MLN CHARGE.

text.p: International film and music company PolyGram NV will report a decline in 1996 profits on Wednesday as it feels the effect of a $90 million restructuring charge.
Analysts expect PolyGram, 75-percent owned by Dutch giant Philips Electronics NV , to post net income of 585-605 million guilders, once the charge is taken into account.
This compares with net income of 741 million guilders in 1995.
PolyGram, which has stock market listings in Amsterdam and New York, said in October that it would cut some 400 jobs worldwide as it restructures its music operations.
It said it expected its operating result before charges to be flat or slightly below the 1995 figure of 1.08 billion guilders, blaming sluggish music sales.

Responding to tougher conditions in a previously buoyant market, PolyGram said it planned to rejuvenate the Motown label, which spawned a raft of classic soul songs in the 1960s and 1970s but has since lost its way.
PolyGram, which acquired Motown in 1993, is moving the company's headquarters from Los Angeles to New York and overhauling its roster of artists.
PolyGram, whose artists include U2, The Cranberries, Bryan Adams and Lionel Richie, said it planned to reorganise its European music distribution and marketing operations.
It is also restructuring a classical music division which boasts the famous Deutsche Grammophon, Decca/London and Philips Classics labels.

The value of the global music industry has grown to around 40 billion dollars in 1995 from 14 billion in 1986. But growth for 1996 was believed to be patchy, with strong increases in Latin America and Asia struggling to offset flat conditions in the more mature markets of the U.S. and Europe.

Analysts say much of the impetus provided in the 1980s by the introduction of compact discs and the Walkman has begun to fade. They point out that there is still heavy demand for the work of the top artists.
But they note that PolyGram's performance has been hampered by delays in its release schedule, notably the failure of U2 to deliver their new album in the second half.

Interest will also centre on PolyGram's infant film division. Its sales grew 32 percent in the first half thanks to hits such as Dead Man Walking and Trainspotting and a 37 million guilder operating loss was described as "on plan".
